scope: Read-only review of sparse action representation, dense-reference tests, and the four production action consumers. No new execution, no whole-tree validation and no performance acceptance.
verdict: no new blocking correctness defect identified in this scope; current-head CI and combined source review remain required

findings.assessment: build_write_actions retains each parsed Add/Update exactly as the old dense map. The original scanned_paths set is passed separately to production dirty reconciliation. Full builds still perform no dirty promotion.

An explicit action takes precedence. A path absent from sparse actions is eligible for old Skip behavior iff the captured scanned_paths inventory contains it. Scoped scans retain surviving off-event DB paths and exclude admitted removals. This preserves the previous dense admission boundary, including scanned but unreadable or unparsed paths.

The unfinished-root test covers the union of explicit actions and scanned_paths, matching prior dense membership. Each promoted implicit Skip is materialized as DirtyResolveOnly before reload and write.

The consumers select Add/Update, Add, DirtyResolveOnly and DirtyResolveOnly respectively. They do not require explicit Skip entries. The changed-files, inventory, reload and write sets therefore retain their membership under the reviewed representation.

The wrapper passing an empty scanned set is cfg(test) and consumes dense actions. Production compute passes real scanned_paths. Retaining the old dense construction under cfg(test) provides a distinct reference implementation.

The added real-DB frontier test compares initial, resume and rebase histories at four budgets, including off-event imports, scanned-unparsed inputs, removed and unadmitted paths, explicit Add and full durable frontier equality. The separate ignored diagnostic times action-map construction and consumers only. This review read these tests; it did not execute them.

limits: No raw wall-clock, memory or whole-build gain is inferred from map sparsity.
The scan inventory, filesystem/hash/resolver work, admission and dirty budgets remain required.
